answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity earn trust like a ship entering a harbor: every new account starts with zero reputation and must do work for several epochs before rewards unlock. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand fake accounts for free, but each pays the full time cost, no bulk discount. If two accounts submit near-identical work, both are penalized together, so cloning answers in the same meadow multiplies the attacker's losses. Trust builds terrace by terrace: each level must be climbed step by step, so fakes cost linear work while honest agents climb once.
